resources.name: Bengali Interfaith Youth Empowerment (BIYE)
resources.mission: BIYE empowers Bengali and South Asian youth ages 13-24 through free, trauma-informed programs rooted in mental health, cultural identity, and interfaith dialogue. Guided by the spirit of seva (selfless service), we foster healing, leadership, and community resilience. Our work centers youth voices to build a more compassionate and inclusive future.

resources.name: Divya Jyoti Jagrati Kendra
resources.mission: We help individuals find inner peace and live their fullest selves through Brahm Gyan, the technique for SelfRealization. The journey begins outward and moves inward, passing through the layers of body, breath, mind, wisdom, and bliss to reach the light of the Soul. Wherever you are on this path, we offer the tools and guidance to support your spiritual growth. Weekly spiritual discourses: Sundays, 11am-1pm. Yoga classes: First Saturday of each month.

resources.name: Practical Knowledge, Inc.
resources.mission: Practical Knowledge, Inc. empowers college-bound students from under-resourced communities with the tools, strategies, and confidence to pursue higher education without unnecessary debt. Our mission is to bridge opportunity gaps by delivering practical, actionable knowledge that drives lasting success in education and beyond.

resources.name: Rabbinical Seminary of America
resources.mission: To educate young people for careers in Jewish Communal Leadership positions. Our alumni graduate with the talents, skills and training to serve the community in every facet of leadership, as teachers, principals, youth workers, chaplains, communal rabbis, and campus college advisors. They currently serve in over 120 communities throughout the USA. We accept young men of the Jewish faith.

resources.name: Samaritan Daytop Village
resources.mission: For 65 years, Samaritan Daytop Village has been improving the quality of life for New Yorkers facing adversity by helping people help themselves. We are nationally recognized for our treatment of substance use disorder as well as for the veteranspecific approach we pioneered. Our continuum of services includes health and mental health care, transitional and supportive housing, educational and vocational assistance, peer-assisted recovery, and specialized programs for adolescents, families, and seniors.

resources.name: Samaritan Daytop Village
resources.mission: For 65 years, Samaritan Daytop Village has been improving the quality of life for New Yorkers facing adversity by helping people help themselves. We are nationally recognized for our treatment of substance use disorder as well as for the veteran-specific approach we pioneered. Our continuum of services includes health and mental health care, transitional and supportive housing, educational and vocational assistance, peerassisted recovery, and specialized programs for adolescents, families, and seniors. Annually, Samaritan Daytop Village serves over 43,000 people at more than 80 programs throughout New York City, Long Island, and the Hudson Valley. Families who want to enroll their children at The Daytop Preparatory School (DPS) must first schedule an appointment for a clinical assessment with an admissions specialist. DPS Admissions can be contacted at 845.353.2730 for Rockland and 631.351.7112 for Suffolk. All calls are confidential.
